text: hey everybody this morning social scientist Dr Samuel Perry posted some findings of research conducted by the American Bible Society on Twitter and I
wanted to share those findings with you This research is a part of abs's state of the Bible from their 2023 report and
this part of the research started with asking participants if they felt the nation would be better off without the
Bible about the same without the Bible or worse off without the Bible and about 14 of the participants said the nation
would be better off without the Bible and then the other 86 percent was about roughly split between about the same and
worse off so on this chart the light blue line that's representative of people who think our nation would be worth off if we did not have the Bible
the red line is those who think the nation would be better off if we did not have the Bible and this is how those
different groups responded to these pro-social questions so this is endorsement of these pro-social
principles welcome immigrants into my community befriend people of other races befriend people of other religions care for those who are in prison care for the
environment advocate for those who are oppressed by society and be a good neighbor many of these not all of these but many of these are explicitly
commanded in the Bible and even in the New Testament and even by Jesus himself but in every single category
the participants who thought the nation would be better off without the Bible endorsed these pro-social principles more than those who felt the nation
would be worse off without the Bible and in a majority of them the participants who thought the nation would be worse
off without the Bible were the ones who endorse these principles the least I think this is a pretty strong indication
that the Bible is being pedestalized not because it is an ethical or a moral
guide or Beacon but because it is an identity marker and I think people are concerned for advancing the interests of
their identity politics more than they are concerned for advancing the interests of their neighbors
